extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and citizens interested in wartime politics
extracted.subtask_description: A historical newspaper report of House of Commons and Lords debates about the conduct of the Norway campaign and wartime government competence. Extracts normative statements and evaluative standards used in the article to judge government, military strategy, and leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air parity / air supremacy is vital
rubrics_metrics.description: Air parity is considered vital to Britain’s security; numerical deficiency in the air has condemned us and will condemn us for some time to come to a great deal of difficulty and suffering and danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article stresses need to produce many more aircraft (“we have to make every effort to give the Air Force many more machines”), to establish fighter bases (capture or establish airdromes), and that lack of fighter bases gave Germans air mastery and contributed to withdrawal from central Norway. Anti-pattern: underestimating enemy air power or deploying without air cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and parliamentary support for effective war prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: No government can prosecute a war efficiently unless it has public and parliamentary support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers urge that governments must retain the confidence of the House and the public; losing that support is presented as rendering war prosecution inefficient. Example: calls for tests of confidence and warnings that the Government no longer commanded Parliament’s confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government accountability and acceptance of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers must accept responsibility for decisions and actions (e.g., Churchill: 'I take the fullest responsibility myself...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting responsibility is contrasted with 'washing hands like Pontius Pilate' as an anti-pattern. The article records Ministers publicly taking responsibility for Admiralty decisions; accountability is framed as necessary in wartime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid precipitous, ill-debated votes on critical war policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Important war matters should not be decided by a precipitate vote ill-debated and on a wide and discursive field but in a grave manner and in due time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism of using an adjournment motion as a de facto vote of no confidence; guidance is to use proper motions and full debate rather than sudden procedural devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh military cost vs advantage (risk management in operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Military strategy must balance the potential gains of an operation against the disproportionate cost and risk (e.g., not sending a battlecruiser to Trondheim because risking a capital ship would be too great a damage to the fleet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-making should consider fleet preservation vs tactical opportunity. Example given: abstaining from sending the only available battlecruiser to avoid risking a major loss; anti-pattern: reckless commitment of irreplaceable assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined action among army, navy, air (inter-service coordination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations should involve combined action between army, navy, and air rather than half-prepared expeditionary forces or isolated efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique of 'half-prepared, half-baked expeditionary force' and calls that 'we ought to have had combined action between the army and the navy.' Emphasizes sending the very best men and integrating services for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate intelligence, reconnaissance, and prior survey
rubrics_metrics.description: Thorough surveying and intelligence (airfields, gasoline dumps, means to check enemy) are required before operations; failure to survey Norway for airdromes and dumps contributed to setbacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers cite failures to survey Norway as a cause of mishandling; guidance implies pre-operation reconnaissance and intelligence are essential. Anti-pattern: launching operations without knowledge of local infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient materiel and logistics (anti-aircraft guns, supplies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective campaigns require adequate logistical support and materiel (e.g., anti-aircraft guns, stores); loss of a ship carrying AA guns produced serious deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes that sinking of a convoy carrying anti-aircraft guns left Britain short; production must ramp up and every effort should be made to supply forces. Example: ship sinkings causing critical shortages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal investigation/inquiry into operational failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Setbacks such as the Norwegian campaign warrant a select committee of inquiry to study causes and mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for a select committee to examine Norway campaign; guidance: use formal, parliamentary inquiry to establish lessons and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain national unity and avoid public political infighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Public displays of political division weaken national position and may encourage the enemy; 'the great thing was to avoid saying anything that might let the Germans think we are a divided people.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers urge setting aside party feuds, letting personal quarrels be forgotten, and harnessing all energies for war effort. Anti-pattern: public shouting, heckling, and partisan grandstanding during crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers must possess initiative, courage, vision, and psychological understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective conduct of foreign policy and war requires ministers with imagination, psychological understanding, liveliness, self-respect, courage and initiative; otherwise they are 'unsuitable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism of ministers as 'lacking courage, initiative' and as 'unsuitable' for wartime leadership. Guidance: choose leaders with these qualities; anti-pattern: timid or complacent leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore and protect national prestige and neutral judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations and conduct should aim to restore Britain’s prestige and prevent adverse neutral judgment resulting from withdrawal or apparent weakness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal's damage is 'very great' in effect on neutral judgment; restoring prestige is presented as necessary for broader strategic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid personalization of national policy; prioritize national interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Debates and decisions should focus on the national interest rather than personal issues or personalities; 'the Government had to face its position with the people and not as personal issues.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers warn against making the Prime Minister's personality inseparable from country’s interest or treating issues as personal quarrels; guidance: keep policy debates substantive and impersonal where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudent conservation of scarce resources when methods are too costly
rubrics_metrics.description: When methods (e.g., surface patrols) become too costly due to enemy strength, alternative methods (submarine blockade) may be adopted pragmatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Churchill: immense enemy air strength made certain patrol methods far too costly; adopted submarine blockade as the only method at disposal. Guidance: adapt tactics to resource constraints and enemy capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seize or deny strategic airfields to enable fighter operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Control of nearby airdromes is essential for fighter operations; lack of bases left fighters vulnerable and grounded, undermining operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: British fighters operating from frozen lake airdrome were bombed and suffered; question raised why capture of an airdrome near Narvik wasn't achieved. Guidance: prioritize capturing/holding air bases to enable operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: War won by hard facts and material effort, not mere prestige
rubrics_metrics.description: Victory depends on tangible resources, production and hard facts rather than prestige or rhetoric: 'the war is going to be won by hard facts and not by prestige.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on production increases, concrete materiel, and realistic assessment rather than public relations. Anti-pattern: relying on prestige or slogans instead of practical measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form a broad-based government when existing administration loses confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If current government no longer commands confidence, the need may arise for a new, broadly based ministry representing parties to prosecute the war effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press and MPs discuss forming a new government broader in composition; guidance: when lacking parliamentary confidence, consider wider coalition for national unity.
